gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Electric Bike Review did not test the Velotric Nomad 2's 1,000 lb towing rating ('remains unverified without a trailer in hand'), and none says which trailer coupler the Nomad 2 needs or what tongue weight it allows.
standout_why: Compared against the cited bicyclingland.com hunting picks (2026-10-03) and the top result sledgeback.com (2026-11-06), plus ChatGPT's own answer. Bicyclingland already gives the XPeak 2.0 60 lb rack limit (from Lectric help text) and the $200 step to the 960 Wh battery. It does not cover which accessories fit which models, and for trailers it only says to ask the trailer maker. Sledgeback says the Nomad 2X is 'the only bike here rated to tow a cart' at 1,000 lb but gives no coupler or hitch details. ChatGPT already quoted the Nomad 2's 66 lb rack and its 1,000 lb towing rating. The new findings are small: a named reviewer did not test the towing figure, and EBR describes the XPeak 2.0's 960 Wh battery as a choice made at purchase. The finding that would have stood out was the maker's coupler compatibility list and tongue-weight limit, but I could not open that page (HTTP 429 or certificate error on every try).
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. For a hunter who plans to haul with a trailer, the 1,000 lb towing figure on the Velotric Nomad 2 and 2X is Velotric's claim only. Electric Bike Review did not test it, and no page I opened names the coupler or a tongue-weight limit. So the page should not make towing the reason to pick the Nomad. Racks are similar across the budget picks: EBR measured nothing but reports a 66 lb rating on the Nomad 2 and 60 lb on the XPeak 2.0. A real stand-and-pack load either fits those racks or needs a trailer the maker has confirmed fits.
